title: Money & Banking · Natural hierarchy of money

concepts.title: An instrument can be money to its holder and credit relative to a higher settlement layer.
A financial claim is an asset of its holder and a liability of its issuer.
Whether a claim is inside or outside depends on the consolidation boundary.
Credit can expand without its issuer creating higher-level settlement money.
Credit quantity and the ease of using credit as money are distinct dimensions.
Market makers maintain conversion between layers at particular prices.
Central-bank policy influences the hierarchy without mechanically controlling every longer-term rate.
An overnight loan lasts one day while its rate is normally quoted on an annual basis.
The currency and banking principles emphasize settlement constraints and credit elasticity respectively.
Longer yields reflect expected future short rates and compensation for risk, rather than today’s policy rate alone.
